title: Python link/adaptive_sf.py density threshold 10 vs ccp.py 8 — dual-selector divergence
description: Follow-up from b7z9.58 audit: python/src/lichen/link/adaptive_sf.py uses density > 10 (lines :16 pseudocode, :137 explicit step-3) while python/src/lichen/ccp.py adaptive_sf_select uses density > 8 (landed b7z9.30.1 per spec 2a.8 = DENSITY_HIGH 8). Two Python selectors for the same spec procedure with different thresholds — cross-impl parity broken (C gradient.c and Rust rf_health.rs both use 8). Verify which is the canonical selector (ccp.py is the spec-pseudocode oracle per ccp16.json vectors; link/adaptive_sf.py may be the runtime path), then align to 8 and reconcile any tests pinning 10. Related: b7z9.58 (closed cannot-reproduce — current spec says >8 in five places).
close_reason: Completed: python density threshold aligned 10 -> 8 across both selectors: (1) link/adaptive_sf.py explicit step-3 branch (:137) + docstring pseudocode (:16) + stale comments (:125-127); (2) ccp.py adaptive_sf_select step-3 (:231) — unconditional per spec 2a.8 (DENSITY_HIGH=8), matching Rust rf_health.rs and the vector generator; (3) stale prose in ccp.py/comment block updated. Vector files synced from main (ccp16.json, ccp16_load_balance.json, generate.py with the full-rule SF derivation; plus 12 main-only vector files restored that my stale branch lacked — announce_length_caps, dtn_sflag_hbh, gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1, srh_admission, schnorr48 schema, etc.) and test_vectors.py assertion aligned to the full AdaptiveSFSelect rule (pseudocode + floors, not table-only). Note: the implicit-table shortcut gate at :129 (density <= 10) remains by design — it gates the non-pseudocode table path only, and no committed vector or caller exercises it (reviewer-verified). 2436+ ccp/adaptive/vector tests pass; ruff clean; 22 lichen-core rust targets green. Scope note: syncing my stale branch's whole test/vectors tree with main is janitor work (b7z9-sync), flagged here because this bead could not be verified without it.
